reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing improper is being proposed to the counterparty.

The cited text supports the compliance conclusion: Section 3.2(a) supplies a quality-of-performance standard (reasonable care / degree of skill and attention applied to comparable receivables under the Servicing Procedures), the Eligibility Representation is made at Closing and each Acquisition Date with express survival of transfer and pledge, and Sections 2.5(b)-(c) / 3.3(b)-(d) supply a cash reacquisition/acquisition remedy at the Acquisition Amount after an uncured material breach — the functional analogue of 'repair, replace or refund'.
No 'AS IS' clause or blanket warranty disclaimer appears in the cited material, so the walk-away trigger is absent and the express representations are not swallowed.

The failed deterministic check (no explicit 90-day/12-month period) is a phrasing artifact of this instrument type: the representations survive open-endedly rather than for a fixed window, which is better than the preferred 12-month/90-day limits for our side, and the rationale expressly notes the point rather than ignoring it.

Non-applicable preferred sub-elements (documentation conformance, malicious code) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, and the willful-misconduct/gross-negligence liability standard is properly deferred to the LOL rule instead of being double-flagged here.
